title: Exact series formulas for the capacities of the amplitude damping channel
abstract: We derive explicit, absolutely convergent series formulas for the quantum, unassisted classical, and entanglement-assisted classical capacities of the qubit amplitude damping channel, eliminating residual optimizations and implicit roots. We also obtain analytical upper and lower bounds on two-way assisted quantum and private communication capacities by evaluating a balanced-squashing bound and optimizing the reverse coherent information. Our results characterize the optimal input populations, establish convergence and truncation properties, and provide analytical benchmarks for quantum and classical communication over dissipative channels.
summary: This paper provides exact, convergent series formulas for calculating the quantum, classical, and entanglement-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude damping channel. By employing advanced mathematical techniques, the authors characterize the limits of information transmission over this common noisy quantum channel. The results offer crucial analytical benchmarks for quantum communication theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive exact, explicit series formulas for the various information-carrying capacities (quantum, classical, entanglement-assisted) of the qubit amplitude damping channel.
main_result: It provides convergent series representations for these capacities, characterizing the optimal input states and establishing analytical bounds for two-way assisted communication.
method: The authors employ advanced techniques including Lagrange-Bürmann inversion, optimization of coherent information, and the use of normalized moment formalisms to derive closed-form series.
model_or_system: The primary model is the qubit amplitude damping channel, $A_\gamma$, which models energy dissipation in a quantum system characterized by the damping probability $\gamma$.
key_observables: Quantum Capacity $Q(A_\gamma)$, Unassisted Classical Capacity $C(A_\gamma)$, Entanglement-Assisted Capacity $CE(A_\gamma)$, and the lower bound for two-way assisted capacity $	ext{RRCI}(\gamma)$.
important_parameters: The damping probability $\gamma$ ($0 \le \gamma \le 1$), and derived parameters like $k = \gamma/(1-2\gamma)$ and optimal input populations $u^*_\gamma$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often restricts optimization to diagonal input states ($ho_u$) and relies on the absolute convergence of the derived series representations.
figures_summary: Not specified in the provided notes, but the structure implies comparisons between derived capacity formulas and known limits at $\gamma=0$ and $\gamma=1/2$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives formulas for different capacities (Quantum, Classical, Entanglement-Assisted) using series expansions, establishes bounds for two-way communication, and analyzes the behavior in different regimes of the damping parameter $\gamma$.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, exact mathematical characterizations of information loss in a fundamental open quantum system (amplitude damping), which is crucial for understanding quantum communication protocols in realistic noisy environments.
